title: Development of Eu3+ Doped MoO3 Nanostructures for Emerging Photovoltaic and Photocatalytic Applications

ABSTRACT

Introducing Eu into the host lattice modifies its electronic structure for improving the power conversion efficiency of hetero-junction solar cells and water-purification technologies. The prepared nanomaterials were well characterized by various spectral techniques viz; XRD, SEM-EDX, TEM, XPS and FT-IR analysis. The phase purity and crystalline structure typically confirming the orthorhombic geometry of Eu-MoO3 nanoparticle using XRD study. XPS characterized the successful incorporation of Eu3+ ions into the lattice and exact chemical valence states of Mo6+/Mo5+ and Eu3+/Eu2+, maps the concentration of oxygen vacancies induced by green combustion. Under Sun-light irradiation, the Eu-MoO3 nanoparticles demonstrated enhanced degradation kinetics against RhB dye than host-MoO3 nanoparticle, which is attributed to efficient charge separation mediated by the Eu3+ dopant states. The degradation efficiencies of host and Eu-MoO3 nanoparticles were found to be 83% and 95% after 165 min under Sun-light irradiation. The fabricated DSSCs were subjected to J-V analysis under a solar simulator to evaluate their photovoltaic performance. The open-circuit voltage of the DSSC fabricated with Eu3+ was found to be 0.687 V, which is higher than host-MoO3 (0.652 V). Eu doped DSSC showed a higher JSC of 4.664 mA/cm2 than host-MoO3 (4.0 mA/cm2). As a result, the power conversion efficiency increased from 0.85% to 1.11% for the Eu-doped DSSCs. This research work offers valuable insights into modifying nanomaterial electronic properties for highly efficient photocatalytic and photovoltaic applications.
